item.title: Jack’s Old-Time Jam — Wed Oct 21, 5:00 PM — Jack Of The Wood
item.description:
Grab some dinner and a pint while enjoying our long-running Old-Time Jam! Featuring many talented musicians from the local WNC area, our traditional Appalachian mountain music jam runs from 5-9pm every Wednesday night at Jack of the Wood! Jack Of The Wood is still a downtown hot spot for food, brews and drink since 1997 and founders Joan and Joe Eckert who still own it, have maintained the original lively English and Irish vibe. The old-time mountain and Irish music jams continue, including a hot bluegrass jam Thursdays and brunch every Sunday. The venue extends a welcoming feeling to regulars and newcomers to this day. https://jackofthewood.com/
Source: LiveMusicAsheville.com

item.title: Jam > Grass > Jam: The Saylor Brothers — Wed Oct 21, 6:30 PM — French Broad River Brewery
item.description:
The Saylor Brothers are a jamgrass fusion group from Asheville, fronted by brothers Will & Ben Saylor, of Brushfire Stankgrass. This project is a foray further into the realm of bluegrass jam, with more emphasis on improvisation piled on top of a structure of traditional bluegrass and innovative original songwriting. As a trio with Greg Stiglets on bass, the band packs a large sound coming from three acoustic instruments, and often adds a fourth player for further improvisational and bluegrass firepower.
Jam > Grass > Jam is not an open bluegrass jam but is a residency featuring a rotating casts of special guests from Asheville’s bluegrass/jamband scene.
French Broad River Brewery is more than just a place to enjoy a drink—it’s a community hub where great beer, delicious pizza, live music, and good times come together. item.title: Peace of Mind — Wed Oct 21, 7:00 PM
item.description:
Meditation in Asheville: Meditation and Modern Buddhism Peace of Mind with Modern Buddhism Teacher Kadam Sharon Lovich Peace is the foundation of our happiness and the good news is this potential for peace already exists within our own mind. In this relaxing series we will explore a variety of simple and practical meditations that will help us slow down, let go of stress and connect with our natural capacity for peace, happiness and a positive outlook. Each class focuses on a different meditation that you can easily bring into your daily life giving you practical tools to create a calmer and happier way of living. Everyone is welcome - no meditation experience required. Cost: $12 (free and online options for members) [Read More and Register](https://www.meditationinasheville.org/wednesday-drop-in-meditation-class-asheville-nc/) [Become a Member](https://www.meditationinasheville.org/become-a-member/)

item.description: The Queen Sessions at Hotel Eve | A celebration of the legendary women who shaped jazz. Each Wednesday evening features a rotating lineup of Asheville’s premier vocalists, each bringing their own style, artistry, and interpretation to the music of legends like Ella Fitzgerald, Billie Holiday, Nina Simone, Sarah Vaughan, Dinah Washington, Abbey Lincoln, and more. item.title: Asheville Crokinole Club — Tue Oct 27, 6:00 PM — Taproom At Highland Brewing Co.
item.description:
Crokinole Tuesdays at Highland Brewing Taproom Join us every Tuesday in the Taproom for an evening of flicks, strategy, and friendly competition! We’re hosting the Asheville Crokinole Club—a community of players who love this classic dexterity board game. Never played? No problem! Crokinole is easy to learn and endlessly fun. Players take turns flicking wooden discs across a circular board, aiming for the high-scoring center zones. The twist? If your opponent has discs on the board, you must hit one—miss, and your piece is out! Whether you’re a seasoned pro or just curious, come grab a pint, meet new friends, and test your skills.
Source: Highland Brewing

item.title: 9:15 Contemplative Service — Sun Nov 1, 9:15 AM — *1 Sanctuary
item.description:
At 9:15 AM, we have a 40-45 minute Contemplative Worship Service. This service invites participants into a reflective, more meditative space, and includes silence, beautiful recorded music and videos, and opportunities for sharing. It also features the sermon and theme which will be the focus in the second service at 11:15 AM. This service is not livestreamed., and it include childcare but not a full religious education program. This service will be particularly good if you need quiet in order to hear well or focus, would prefer a little more space around you, or seek a more contemplative communal experience. Between services, at 10 am we will have coffee hour and special programs. Whether you come to the early service or the later service, we encourage you to consider arriving at 10 am for coffee, conversation, and special programs including conversations with the Board, or Minister & lay-led justice or adult education offerings.
Source: Unitarian Universalist Congregation of Ashevi

**Here's how it works.** Show up at or before 6:00. At 6:00, we do some quick introductions. Afterward, for a full 60 minutes (I'll set a timer!) we are heads-down writing. Writing what? A novel? You bet. Some poetry? Sure. Song lyrics? Your resume? That report you need to get to your boss before 8 AM or you'll *need* *to write* that resume? All of the above and more. Just shut up and write.
Surrounding ourselves with other writers who are busy putting words onto page (physical or virtual) keeps us all accountable and focused.

item.title: Peace of Mind — Wed Nov 11, 7:00 PM
item.description:
Meditation in Asheville: Meditation and Modern Buddhism Peace of Mind with Modern Buddhism Teacher Kadam Sharon Lovich Peace is the foundation of our happiness and the good news is this potential for peace already exists within our own mind. In this relaxing series we will explore a variety of simple and practical meditations that will help us slow down, let go of stress and connect with our natural capacity for peace, happiness and a positive outlook. Each class focuses on a different meditation that you can easily bring into your daily life giving you practical tools to create a calmer and happier way of living. Everyone is welcome - no meditation experience required. Cost: $12 (free and online options for members) [Read More and Register](https://www.meditationinasheville.org/wednesday-drop-in-meditation-class-asheville-nc/) [Become a Member](https://www.meditationinasheville.org/become-a-member/)
Source: Meditation in Asheville

item.title: Fun & easy way to play more tennis (please read event description for details) — Thu Nov 12, 7:00 PM
item.description:
PlayYourCourt Asheville Tennis We’re still working to get more people into these Meetups, but our goal is to give PlayYourCourt members a few social tennis outings each week in addition to your practice sessions and Challenge League matches.
These Meetups are co-ed, super laid back, and all skill levels are welcome. Post your skill level and a suggested court in the comments section so we can round up as many players as we can for some tennis fun!
Also, if you’re looking to meet new practice partners or play some matches and you aren’t already in the PlayYourCourt Community, you can go here to see what we’re all about and sign up:
https://www.playyourcourt.com/tennis-community/asheville-nc/meetup/
If you love tennis, we’d love to have you! Be sure and watch the quick video that explains how everything works.
Happy hitting!
- Scott
Source: PlayYourCourt Asheville Tennis

item.title: Birding for Beginners — Tue Dec 1, 9:00 AM
item.description: Birding for Beginners with Shane Myers Tuesday, December 1 | 9 – 10:30am BRN – Elective Register Here! Join us on this birding walk around the NC Arboretum gardens and trails in search of our most colorful residents. We will go over best practices for using binoculars, recommendations for purchasing your own binoculars, and popular field guides to use. Bring your own binoculars but if you do not have a pair we have some loaner binoculars available to use during the programs. This program will take place outside and will follow easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time. Shane Myers’ interest in nature began as a child with a love of dinosaurs. This quickly grew to include fossils, insects, and reptiles, and learning from the notes his grandparents kept of the birds that came to their feeders in Toledo, Ohio.
